answer: At each epoch's dawn each identity files a signed forecast of three figures: attestations, authors, pool size. Settlement scores it by squared error and merges identities with near-identical twelve-epoch forecasts into one cluster, paid as one head with weight split among members. Copying one model to a thousand keys earns one share split a thousand ways; random guesses break correlation but wreck accuracy, so weight hits zero. Earning N shares needs N independent observers, each a surveyor on its own knoll seeing different traffic. No shared cipher replaces that per-head information cost.
